proof.text: Put $r_n(i)=n-i$ and $\alpha^\vee=r_n\alpha r_m$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Since $(\alpha\beta)^\vee=\alpha^\vee\beta^\vee$ and $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$, the degreewise opposite construction in the statement is a covariant involution on simplicial sets and maps. There is an isomorphism $\Delta^n\cong(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ sending a degree-$k$ simplex $\theta:[k]\to[n]$ to $r_n\theta r_k$. It takes the horn missing face $i$ to the horn missing face $n-i$, since omission of vertex $j$ becomes omission of vertex $n-j$. Thus any inner-horn problem in $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ reverses to the inner horn with index $n-i$ in $\mathcal D$, has a filler there, and reverses back to a filler. In particular $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. The same argument, allowing all horn indices, shows that opposite preserves Kan complexes. The horn and Kan conventions used here are exactly those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Opposite-category dual of Proposition 4.6.5.10; explicit horn reversal

proof.text: Write $A=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(b,a)$, using the right-pinched convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Reversing a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{m+1}\to\mathcal D$ means taking its opposite and precomposing with $\Delta^{m+1}\cong(\Delta^{m+1})^{\mathrm{op}}$ from step 1. A simplex in $L_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ then has its initial face constant at $b$ and its last vertex $a$, so this gives a degreewise bijection with $A$. It is a simplicial isomorphism $\Phi:L_{\mathcal D}(a,b)\cong A^{\mathrm{op}}$: if $\alpha^L:[k+1]\to[m+1]$ fixes $0$ and sends $i+1$ to $\alpha(i)+1$, direct evaluation at $i\leq k$ and at $k+1$ gives $(\alpha^L)^\vee=(\alpha^\vee)^+$, where $(-)^+$ extends a map by sending the new last vertex to the new last vertex. This is precisely the right-pinched operator for $\alpha^\vee$, that is, the $\alpha$-operator of $A^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversal twice is the identity, so the bijections and their inverses respect every face and degeneracy.

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX) and opposite reversal of pinched simplices

proof.text: Write $B=U_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(b,a)$, with $U$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. A degree-$m$ simplex of $U_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ is a map $h:\Delta^m\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal D$ constant at $a,b$ on the two endpoint layers. Apply opposite to $h$ and reverse both standard-simplex factors as in step 1. Products are degreewise, so the resulting map into $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is constant at $b,a$ on the two layers. This gives a bijection $\Psi_m$ to $B_m$. For a parameter operator $\alpha$, reversing $\alpha\times\mathrm{id}$ gives $\alpha^\vee\times\mathrm{id}$, hence $\Psi_m$ assemble to a simplicial isomorphism $\Psi:U_{\mathcal D}(a,b)\cong B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Again reversing twice is the inverse. Swapping the product factors identifies these formulas with the internal-functor convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.7 (01L2), with explicit reversal of the ordinary arrow fiber

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_m(i,0)=0$, $\lambda_m(i,1)=i+1$ be the left-pinch order map, and let $\rho_m(i,0)=i$, $\rho_m(i,1)=m+1$ be the right-pinch order map of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. For every monotone $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$, $\lambda_m(\alpha\times\mathrm{id})=\alpha^L\lambda_k$: both sides are $0$ on the lower layer and $\alpha(i)+1$ on the upper layer. Thus $j^L$ is simplicial. Moreover,
$$r_{m+1}\rho_m(r_m(i),1-t)=\lambda_m(i,t)\quad(t=0,1),$$
since the left side is respectively $0$ and $i+1$. The two maps agree as maps of the product poset, so their nerve maps agree in every simplicial degree. Consequently the isomorphisms just constructed satisfy $\Psi j^L=(j_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}},b,a})^{\mathrm{op}}\Phi$. This proves the claimed identification of the actual specified maps, not merely an equivalence between their sources and targets.

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.7 (01L2); conjugation identity for the two explicit pinch maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] to the quasicategory $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its vertices $b,a$. It says that $A,B$ are Kan complexes and $j:A\to B$ is a homotopy equivalence. Step 1 makes $A^{\mathrm{op}},B^{\mathrm{op}}$ Kan. If $g:B\to A$ is a homotopy inverse of $j$, its opposite is an inverse up to homotopy of $j^{\mathrm{op}}$: applying opposite to either cylinder homotopy and using the degreewise product identity gives a homotopy with parameter $(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}$; precompose with the simplex-reversal isomorphism $\Delta^1\cong(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}$. This only interchanges the two homotopy endpoints, and yields the required homotopies between $g^{\mathrm{op}}j^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the identity and between $j^{\mathrm{op}}g^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the identity. If homotopies are expressed as finite chains of cylinder homotopies, apply this operation to each member of the chain. The isomorphisms and equality of step 4 therefore give the claimed homotopy equivalence $j^L$ of Kan complexes. This argument also covers empty mapping complexes; it never chooses a vertex in either fiber.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, right-handed assertion applied to the opposite quasicategory; explicit reversal of inverse homotopies

proof.text: For a simplicial functor $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ with $F(a)=a'$ and $F(b)=b'$, postcomposition sends left-pinched simplices and fixed-endpoint arrow simplices to the corresponding simplices with endpoints $a',b'$. On every degree-$m$ simplex $\sigma$, associativity of composition gives $F(\sigma\lambda_m)=(F\sigma)\lambda_m$. Thus $U(F)j^L_{\mathcal D,a,b}=j^L_{\mathcal D',a',b'}L(F)$ strictly in each degree, proving the requested naturality. No choice of homotopy inverse enters this equation.

title: Natural comparison of left-pinched and arrow mapping spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and the right-pinched mapping space of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the right-pinch equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ and vertices $a,b$, define the left-pinched mapping space $L_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ degreewise: an $m$-simplex is a map $\Delta^{m+1}\to\mathcal D$ whose vertex $0$ is $a$ and whose restriction to the final face on vertices $1,\ldots,m+1$ is the constant simplex at $b$; simplicial operators are induced by the corresponding order maps fixing the first vertex. Let $U_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ be the fixed-endpoint arrow space of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Precomposition in degree $m$ with the map $\Delta^m\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^{m+1}$ induced by $(i,0)\mapsto0$ and $(i,1)\mapsto i+1$ (interchanging the two product factors to use the internal-functor convention) defines the left-pinch map
$$j^L_{\mathcal D,a,b}:L_{\mathcal D}(a,b)\longrightarrow U_{\mathcal D}(a,b).$$
Equivalently, let $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ have the same $n$-simplices, with the operator of $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ given by the operator of $i\mapsto n-\alpha(k-i)$ on $\mathcal D$; then reversing simplices identifies $L_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ and $U_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ with the opposites of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(b,a)$ and $U_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(b,a)$, and $j^L_{\mathcal D,a,b}$ with the opposite of the right-pinch map $j_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}},b,a}$.
This map is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes, natural under every simplicial functor carrying the two specified vertices to the specified endpoints.
